Mikołaj Firlej was a Polish-Lithuanian nobleman, military commander, and statesman who lived from 1588 to 1635. He was born into the influential Firlej family, which had a long history of service to the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

Firlej served as a hetman (commander-in-chief) of the Polish army during the Polish-Swedish War of 1626-1629. He distinguished himself in this conflict by leading successful military campaigns against the Swedish forces and securing several key victories for the Commonwealth.

In addition to his military career, Firlej also held various important political positions. He served as a senator in the Polish-Lithuanian Sejm (parliament) and was appointed voivode (province governor) of Lublin in 1630.

Firlej was known for his loyalty to the Commonwealth and his dedication to defending its interests. He was also a supporter of religious tolerance and advocated for the rights of Protestant minorities within the predominantly Catholic state.

Mikołaj Firlej died in 1635 at the age of 47. He is remembered as a skilled military leader, a devoted patriot, and a committed public servant who made significant contributions to the history of Poland and Lithuania.
